audit.whatIsWrong: Kayle's passive is called "Transcendence" throughout — spikes[2] "Kayle hits full-ranged form with Transcendence", wants.you[2] "so she never reaches Transcendence", wants.foe[0] "let Kayle's passive Zeal stacks build naturally toward Transcendence", early "she has short range before Transcendence", late "Once Kayle hits level 11 Transcendence", whys[3] "building toward Transcendence safely", whys[6] "Full Transcendence Kayle".
audit.why: Her passive is Divine Ascent. Transcendence is a Sorcery rune, not a Kayle ability, so the entry is naming a rune as the enemy champion's defining mechanic in seven places. The associated "passive Zeal stacks" is wrong twice over: Zeal is an item, and Divine Ascent has no stack mechanic at all — it scales with LEVELS AND SKILL POINTS SPENT, progressively granting attack speed, move speed, attack range and eventually waves of fire on her attacks. That difference is actionable rather than cosmetic. A stack bar can be denied by refusing her trades; a level-and-points threshold cannot be denied at all, only outpaced. The entry's plan of 'deny her CS so she never reaches Transcendence' is therefore built on a mechanic that does not exist — her form arrives on schedule whatever Tahm Kench does to her gold.
audit.corrected: Divine Ascent, scaling on levels and skill points spent. No stacks, no Zeal, nothing to deny.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kayle.json — P Divine Ascent: 'Kayle's attacks are empowered by the heavens as she levels up and spends skill points. Her wings are lit aflame as she progressively gains Attack Speed, Move Speed, Attack Range, and waves of fire on her attacks.'

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] instructs the player to "punish her stepping up for CS with a stun into Devour before level 6". The same pre-6 Devour appears in spikes[1] (stage Lvl 2-3), early ("land the empowered stun and Devour... She has no dash and no invulnerability at level 2") and whys[2].
audit.why: Devour IS the level-6 ability, so 'stun into Devour before level 6' is self-contradicting in a single sentence. This entry then compounds it: whys[2] calls the pre-6 Devour combo "your only real kill window in the lane", and the whole strategic frame of the matchup is 'win before she scales'. So the file identifies the correct strategy and then hangs it entirely on a button the player does not own during the window it tells him to use it. Against Kayle that is expensive — the early levels genuinely are Tahm Kench's, and a player who steps up expecting a removal and gets only a stun will misjudge how much health he can spend on it.
audit.corrected: Pre-6 the payoff is the Tongue Lash stun plus autos. That is still enough to bully her; it is not a removal.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour is the ultimate slot; P 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice, and that is accurate — the entry contains no numbers at all. mid says she "can burn her R to survive your one clean all-in attempt" and late says she "burns R", but never says what burning it costs her.
audit.why: Divine Judgment is 160/120/80 seconds. At rank 1 that is the longest cooldown either champion has by a factor of three, and it is the single most important sequencing fact in the matchup: if Kayle spends R to survive a Devour, Tahm Kench owns the next 160 seconds outright — enough for a full wave cycle, a dive with the jungler, or a tower. Telling the player to 'bait it' without telling him what he wins by baiting it is why this entry has no actionable trading plan. Her other cooldowns matter less but are worth the contrast: Radiant Blast 12s at rank 1, Celestial Blessing a flat 15s, Starfire Spellblade 8s.
audit.corrected: State the 160s rank-1 Divine Judgment cooldown as the prize for baiting it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kayle.json — R cooldown 160/120/80, Q 12/11/10/9/8, W 15, E 8/7.5/7/6.5/6

audit.whatIsWrong: Kayle's ranged threat is described only as generic "bolts" — "eating autos and E bolts you cannot answer", "Poke with her Q bolts", "her bolt range begins outpacing your safe Q range", "E-empowered burst".
audit.why: Neither ability is a bolt and the range claim is wrong. Radiant Blast (Q) is a 900-range celestial sword that pierces through enemies — the same 900 as Tongue Lash, so it does not out-range him at all. Starfire Spellblade (E) is 550 range and is an attack empowerment, not a poke tool. What actually out-ranges Tahm Kench as the game goes on is her ATTACK range from Divine Ascent, which is a different thing entirely and cannot be dodged. Naming them also surfaces the mechanic that explains the whole late game and which the entry never mentions: Radiant Blast REDUCES THE RESISTANCES of everything it hits, and Starfire Spellblade deals bonus damage proportional to MISSING HEALTH. Those two together are precisely why a tank loses to Kayle at two items — not the vague 'shred through Thick Skin' the entry offers.
audit.corrected: Radiant Blast (Q, 900 range) pierces and cuts resistances; Starfire Spellblade (E, 550) is an auto-empowerment scaling on missing health; the growing range is Divine Ascent's attack range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kayle.json — Q Radiant Blast: 'pierces through enemies, slowing, damaging, and reducing the resistances of all hit', range 900; E Starfire Spellblade: 'Kayle's next attack smites her target with celestial fire, dealing bonus damage proportionate to their missing health', range 550. champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Q range 900

audit.whatIsWrong: Celestial Blessing is never mentioned in either layer, and anti-heal is never raised despite this being the flagged missing interaction for the matchup.
audit.why: Kayle heals herself and the nearest ally on a flat 15-second cooldown. In a lane the entry frames as an attrition race between her chip damage and Thick Skin's grey-health recovery, a 15s heal on her side is the variable that settles it, and it is the reason the early-game window closes faster than the entry implies. Grievous Wounds timing is a real decision here, not boilerplate.
audit.corrected: Name Celestial Blessing and put anti-heal in the plan.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kayle.json — W Celestial Blessing: 'heals and grants Move Speed to herself and the nearest ally', cooldown 15, flag heal; _missing-interactions.json rule needs-antiheal for tahmkench vs kayle

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says "At level 6 your Abyssal Voyage gives you global pressure and the threat of TP-flanks" and later "roam threats via your ultimate".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-2021-rework ultimate and is not on the live champion; Tahm Kench has no global and no TP-flank threat from his kit. The sentence is also self-defeating as written, since it concedes in the same breath that the phantom ability 'does not improve your 1v1 against Kayle'. Level 6 is Devour, which is the one thing that does change the 1v1 — and which trades directly against her Divine Judgment.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour versus her Divine Judgment. That is the actual level-6 interaction.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour, no global ability in kit

audit.why: 50.73% over 613 games with a level chart that hands Kayle everything from Levels 4-5 onward and gives the early stages to Skill. That shape is right for a scaling matchup and matches an even headline number produced by Tahm Kench winning early and losing late. No change proposed.

edits.before: Kayle is legitimately bad at level 1 and 2 — she has short range before Transcendence and no real escape, so you can use Tongue Lash's long slow to contest every CS she tries to take near the front of the wave. The key window is the moment she steps into Q range: slow her, auto twice to stack An Acquired Taste, then land the empowered stun and Devour to remove her completely from the trade. She has no dash and no invulnerability at level 2, so this full combo is lethal for her HP bar. Activate Thick Skin if she gets a Q bolt trade in — your grey health means her poke costs you almost nothing as long as you can idle back briefly between trades.
edits.after: Kayle is legitimately bad at level 1 and 2 — Divine Ascent has barely started, she is still melee-range and has no escape, so use Tongue Lash's long slow to contest every CS she tries to take near the front of the wave. The key window is the moment she steps up: slow her, auto twice to stack An Acquired Taste, then land the stun. Devour is your ultimate and is not here yet, but she has no dash and no invulnerability at 2, so the stun plus autos still costs her a third of her bar. Activate Thick Skin if she lands a Radiant Blast — grey health means her poke costs you almost nothing if you idle back between trades.

edits.before: Level 4 and 5 are where she starts to pull away in comfort. She gains more range on her bolts and can begin farming freely without walking into Tongue Lash, so you stop generating free stacks and shift into pure CS mode. At level 6 your Abyssal Voyage gives you global pressure and the threat of TP-flanks, but it does not improve your 1v1 against Kayle — she simply walks away from your slow if she sees it coming, and she can burn her R to survive your one clean all-in attempt. Play these levels for wave equity, roam threats via your ultimate, and make sure you are not behind in CS when her level 11 arrives.
edits.after: Level 4 and 5 are where she starts to pull away in comfort. Divine Ascent keeps adding attack range and she can farm without walking into Tongue Lash, so you stop generating free stacks and shift into pure CS mode. Note Radiant Blast is 900, exactly your Q range, so she never out-ranges the ability itself — only her autos. At 6 your Devour meets her Divine Judgment, and that trade is the whole level: if she burns R to survive it, she has no answer for 160 seconds, which is a dive, a tower or a full wave cycle. Make her spend it, then cash the window in immediately.

edits.before: Once Kayle hits level 11 Transcendence and her first two items, this lane is hers and you know it. Her ranged autos and E-empowered burst shred through Thick Skin faster than you regenerate it, and her R invulnerability means your Devour window — the only tool that wins you a fight — gets voided on demand. Your job past this point is not to 1v1 her; it is to position as a peel-and-disruption frontliner in teamfights, use Devour to deny her the clean back-line access she needs, and let your team collapse on her while she burns R. Win by denying her that clean fight, not by trying to solo-kill her again.
edits.after: Once Divine Ascent is fully online and her first two items land, this lane is hers and you know it. Radiant Blast cuts your resistances and Starfire Spellblade scales on your missing health, which is exactly why stacking HP stops saving you, and her R voids the Devour window on demand. Your job past this point is not to 1v1 her; it is to position as a peel-and-disruption frontliner, use Devour to deny her clean back-line access, and let your team collapse while she burns R. Anti-heal matters too, since Celestial Blessing heals her on a flat 15s cooldown.

notes: "Transcendence" as Kayle's passive is worth a project-wide grep — it is a Sorcery RUNE name, so if the generator confused rune names with ability names once it may have done so elsewhere, and a rune name will never be caught by the packet's suspectNames detector (which scores only against the champion's own kit). Same for "Zeal stacks", where an item name was turned into a champion mechanic. This entry is also the clearest single illustration of why the pre-6 Devour defect is worth a scripted fix rather than tolerance: wants.you[0] literally reads "a stun into Devour before level 6", which contradicts itself inside one sentence, and yet the packet reported only 'no cooldown-sequencing advice' and three suspect names for this matchup. Both flagged defects for kayle were accurate and are addressed above — the sequencing gap is filled with Divine Judgment's 160s rank-1 cooldown as the concrete 'bait X, then you have 160 seconds to do Y' line, and all five of her abilities are now named.
